fields.System.Title: FDN-1 — Service skeleton
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

A service that starts, reports that it is healthy, reads its settings from the environment, and
fails the same way every time something goes wrong.

Scope

In. Health endpoint, environment configuration, structured logging with correlation IDs,
one consistent error response shape.

Out. Any business behaviour. Metrics and tracing — add those when there is something worth
measuring.

Design notes

Build the error shape before the second endpoint. Once there are twenty endpoints returning
errors in twenty formats, nobody goes back and unifies them, and every client ends up with
special cases.

The correlation ID is generated at the edge and travels through logs, events, and audit
rows. It looks like overhead until the first production incident, when it is the difference
between a five-minute trace and a lost afternoon.

Health checks come in two kinds. Liveness — is the process up. Readiness — can it reach the
database. Compose and any future orchestrator need both, and confusing them causes restart
loops.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Silent config defaults produce baffling failures later | [doc 10 §7](../../../docs/10-local-deployment.md) |
| Inconsistent errors force client special-casing | — |
